table_title: List the 36 hosted World Expos since 1851 per Wikipedia's `World's fair` master article's 'World Expos' table (excluding Specialised Expos + Horticultural Expos + cancelled-during-WW expos + scheduled-future Expo 2030 Riyadh). Universe spans 1851 Great Exhibition London through 2025 Osaka. Schema = composite PK (Year, Host City) + Country + Dates + Theme, all cells master-table-verbatim per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4. Country cells stage visible master table text per audit-cycle-2 ruling — visible-master-text rule consistent across all 36 rows. Two rows happen to use period-accurate labels in visible master text (Austria-Hungary 1873; Colony of Victoria 1880); other 34 rows use plain country names including the 3 cycle-2-corrected rows (1929 Barcelona = Spain; 1937 Paris = France; 1949 Port-au-Prince = Haiti — previously staged with flag-link wikitext metadata labels). Sort = Year ASC chronological (master-native).
db_analog: SELECT e.year, e.host_city, e.country, e.dates, e.theme FROM world_expos_master e WHERE e.expo_type = 'World Expo' AND e.host_status = 'hosted' AND e.year >= 1851 ORDER BY e.year ASC, e.host_city ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'World's fair' master article accessed 2026-05-20. Universe = 36 hosted World Expos per the master's 'World Expos' table (rows 1-36 chronologically 1851-2025; row 37 Expo 2030 Riyadh excluded as scheduled-future-not-yet-hosted per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1). The master article has 3 chronological tables: World Expos (focus of this instance), Specialised Expos (NOT in scope), and Horticultural Expos (NOT in scope). Vancouver 1986 is excluded because it appears under Specialised Expos in the master, not World Expos. Cancelled expos (Tokyo 1940, Rome 1942) are not in the master's hosted World Expos table and remain out of scope per audit-cycle-1 amendment #3. Pre-BIE rows (19, through 1915 San Francisco) + BIE-era rows (17, 1929 Barcelona through 2025 Osaka) = 36 total. temporal_sensitivity = medium because the next confirmed World Expo (Expo 2030 Riyadh, hosted 2030-2031) will extend the universe to 37 when hosted. Source priority: master's World Expos table cells supply all 5 staged columns (Year, Host City via Location column, Country via Location column's state-party label, Dates, Theme). Country cells stage VISIBLE MASTER TABLE country text (NOT flag-link wikitext metadata) per audit-cycle-2 ruling. Two rows happen to use period-accurate labels in visible master text: Austria-Hungary (1873 Vienna) and Colony of Victoria (1880 Melbourne). Three cycle-0 rows initially used flag-link-target labels (Restoration (Spain) / French Third Republic / Republic of Haiti 1859-1957) but were corrected in cycle-2 to plain country names (Spain / France / Haiti) matching the visible master text. Other 31 rows use modern country names. Rule is consistent: stage visible-master-text only. Schema = 5 cols with composite PK (Year, Host City) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 — the master table does NOT display an explicit Expo-name column (master uses just Year + Location + Dates + Theme structure with Expo names appearing only via row-link-target metadata), so the composite (Year, Host City) PK avoids per-row link-target extraction. Theme cells preserve master verbatim including italicization-removed text (master uses italics for Theme cells; staged text drops italics formatting but preserves the text including punctuation like the period in 'The independence among Industry and scientific research.').
_extraction_notes: Temporal instance — chronological enumeration of World Expos since 1851 per master's 'World Expos' table inclusion. PIVOT context: 4th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target after multiple set_filter source-friction attempts (canals duplicate; lighthouses fragmented; IGOs fragmented; UNESCO Danger List 403; glaciers fragmented). World expositions has the cleanest tool-friendly canonical Wikipedia master. Brings `temporal` from 5/5 (floor met, just-saturated by existing 5 instances: summer_olympics_hosts_1960_2020 + time_person_of_the_year_2000_2024 + eurozone_adoptions_1999_2023 + nber_dated_us_recessions_since_1929 + phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age) to **6/5** = 4th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target (after epidemics-1M lifting comparative + WWI battles lifting multi_hop + industrial-disasters lifting causal). History/Cultural Events NEW subdomain per audit-cycle-1 per-question ruling — Culture/Heritage existing was an alternative but audit picked History/Cultural Events because expos are HOSTED EVENTS not heritage properties. events/world-expositions NEW fine-class within events bucket extending 13→14 fine-classes (joining space-missions, financial-crises, epidemics, space-incidents, judicial-decisions, olympics, awards, inventions, battles, empires, recessions, pandemics, industrial-disasters). Schema: 5 cols (Year + Host City composite PK + Country + Dates + Theme) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 — master table does NOT have explicit Expo-name column; composite PK (Year, Host City) avoids per-row link-target extraction. BIE Classification column DROPPED per audit-cycle-1 amendment #5 — not a master table column; Pre-BIE vs BIE-era distinction documented in decision_log only. Audit-cycle-1 amendments applied: (1) universe = 36 hosted World Expos 1851-2025 (excludes scheduled-future Expo 2030 Riyadh); (2) exact count 36 (NOT '~30+' from cycle-0); (3) cancelled expos (Tokyo 1940, Rome 1942) NOT staged per master's hosted-only universe; (4) composite PK (Year, Host City) + 5-col schema with master-visible columns; (5) BIE Classification dropped from CSV. Per-question rulings applied: scope = World Expos table only; Theme included (master-native); Country period-accurate; Sort = Year ASC chronological; Domain = History/Cultural Events; entity class = events/world-expositions NEW; claim_type = source_defined; operation_type = filter; temporal_sensitivity = medium. Pre-BIE rows count = 19 (1851 London through 1915 San Francisco); BIE-era rows = 17 (1929 Barcelona through 2025 Osaka); total = 36 ✓. Country visible-master-text rule (post-cycle-2 corrections): 1873 Austria-Hungary; 1880 Colony of Victoria (both period-accurate AND visible master text); 1929 Barcelona Spain; 1937 Paris France; 1949 Port-au-Prince Haiti (plain country names per visible master text; cycle-0 had flag-link wikitext metadata labels which were corrected in cycle-2). Year-anchor accessed 2026-05-20.
